subject: RESERVE clause (number of input-output areas, if not specified)
notes: NOW (kb/Work PB3334, INDEXED on the keyed store engine): the INDEXED organization moved to the keyed store engine (kb/Work PB3334; DESIGN-runtime-library 2.2.1.4): the input-output areas are the page cache's floor for both organizations, sized in KeyedConnector.Attach (2.2.1.13); the whole store's transfer buffer went with it. A.1 item 164 required + documented. cite.py --check 12.4.5.14.3 "If the RESERVE clause is not specified, the number of input-output areas allocated is specified by the implementor" -> OK §12.4.5.14.3 1). Determination (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-164, rewritten by kb/Work PB643, wave 1020 B): one input-output area of 4,096 bytes per connector when the clause is absent (HostFile.ImplementorInputOutputAreas = 1), the ONE buffer between the record area and the medium in every sharing posture (the former 'no input-output area when another writer is admitted' exception is gone: the areas exist in every posture, and the posture decides only when they are emptied). The posture decides only when the areas are emptied, and no program can tell: a connector that admits no other connector (SHARING WITH NO OTHER) fills its areas and flushes at CLOSE; one whose sharing mode admits a reader or a writer (AdmitsAnotherRunUnit) releases each record at its WRITE (GR12). kb/Work PB1587 RETIRED the earlier witness (pb643_reserve_areas_visibility read 064/064/000 of 100 before the CLOSE): it expected a SHARING WITH READ ONLY writer's records to wait in its area, which left sequential and relative answering one program two ways; the case now pins that RESERVE's count changes nothing a sibling reader sees (100 in every phase, 100 after CLOSE). The count is witnessed by its one sizing site (SharedReadCoherenceDriftTests.TheConnectorKeepsOneBuffer_ItsInputOutputAreas_SizedInOnePlace), the round trip through the areas on every organization (pb643_reserve_areas_all_organizations) and the '30' of an OPEN that cannot allocate them. || kb/Work PB2693 (w1045d): a relative or indexed connector's areas are no longer its store handle's stream buffer, which no store byte passed through (the load and the persist are positional, PB2660), so RESERVE allocated memory nothing used; they are KeyedConnector._areas, allocated by the OPEN that takes the file lock (TakeFileLock) and passed through by every load and persist (KeyedConnector.Attach), with the store handle unbuffered (HostFile.OpenConnectorStore). retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/KeyedConnector.cs#ReadThroughAreas (moved with the whole-store model into IndexedConnector.WholeStore.cs, the INDEXED organization's until kb/Work PB3334 (kb/Work PB3333)) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/KeyedConnector.cs#WriteThroughAreas (moved with the whole-store model into IndexedConnector.WholeStore.cs, the INDEXED organization's until kb/Work PB3334 (kb/Work PB3333)) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/IndexedConnector.WholeStore.cs#ReadThroughAreas (the INDEXED organization moved to the keyed store engine (kb/Work PB3334; DESIGN-runtime-library 2.2.1.4): the input-output areas are the page cache's floor for both organizations, sized in KeyedConnector.Attach (2.2.1.13); the whole store's transfer buffer went with it) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/IndexedConnector.WholeStore.cs#WriteThroughAreas (the INDEXED organization moved to the keyed store engine (kb/Work PB3334; DESIGN-runtime-library 2.2.1.4): the input-output areas are the page cache's floor for both organizations, sized in KeyedConnector.Attach (2.2.1.13); the whole store's transfer buffer went with it)
